extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements and examiner guidance for petitions to revive abandoned patent applications (37 CFR 1.137) and related matters (terminal disclaimers, timing, burden of proof, provisional applications, public access, file ordering, notices, and interviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement that entire delay was unintentional for 37 CFR 1.137 petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.137(b)(4) requires that a petition under 37 CFR 1.137 must be accompanied by a statement that the entire delay in providing the required reply from the due date for the reply until the filing of a grantable petition pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137 was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where there is a question whether the delay was unintentional the Director may require additional information. Applicants filing a petition more than two years after abandonment must provide additional explanation establishing that the entire delay was unintentional (in addition to the required statement). Failure to carry the burden of proof that the 'entire' delay was 'unintentional' may lead to denial of the petition regardless of other circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional explanation required for petitions filed more than two years after abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Any applicant filing a petition to revive an abandoned application under 37 CFR 1.137 more than two years after the date of abandonment is required to provide an additional explanation of the circumstances surrounding the delay that establishes that the entire delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This additional explanation is in addition to the statement that the entire delay was unintentional. Electronic ePetition processing options exist for certain petition types (see ePetition list).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ePetition for certain revival-related petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic petitions that are automatically processed and immediately decided may be filed using the web-based ePetition process for specified petition types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Types eligible for ePetition include: (1) Petitions to Accept Late Payment of Issue Fee - Unintentional Late Payment (37 CFR 1.137(a)); (2) Petitions for Revival based on Failure to Notify Office of a Foreign/International Filing (37 CFR 1.137(f)); (3) Petitions for Revival for Continuity Purposes Only (37 CFR 1.137(a)); and (4) Petitions for Revival of an Abandoned Patent Application Abandoned Unintentionally (37 CFR 1.137(a)). Applicants may use Office forms (PTO/SB/64, PTO/SB/64a, PTO/SB/64PCT). See www.uspto.gov/Epetitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three delay periods to consider in 1.137 petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three periods to be considered during evaluation of a petition under 37 CFR 1.137: (A) the delay in reply that originally resulted in the abandonment; (B) the delay in filing an initial petition pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137 to revive the application; and (C) the delay in filing a grantable petition pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137 to revive the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of unintentionality must consider the entire time from the original due date through filing of a grantable petition; different periods may raise different evidentiary concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intentional abandonment/deliberate decision bars finding of unintentional delay
rubrics_metrics.description: The abandonment of an application that was a deliberately chosen course of action, or a deliberate choice not to seek or persist in seeking revival (including deliberate delay to seek revival), is not 'unintentional' within the meaning of 37 CFR 1.137 and precludes a finding of unintentional delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent changes in circumstances, correctness of prior Office decisions, or discovery of new information after the abandonment do not convert a prior deliberate decision into an unintentional delay. Example given: delaying revival until industry or a competitor shows interest is the antithesis of 'unintentional'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office presumption when petition filed within 3 months of first notice and within 1 year of abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office does not generally question whether there has been intentional delay when a petition under 37 CFR 1.137 is filed (A) within 3 months of the date the applicant is first notified that the application is abandoned; and (B) within 1 year of the date of abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are advised to file within 3 months of first notification of abandonment to avoid intentional-delay questions; filing within these timeframes ordinarily avoids further scrutiny of unintentionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may require additional information if petition not filed within 3 months of first notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a petition pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137 is not filed within 3 months of the date the applicant is first notified that the application is abandoned, the Office may consider there to be a question as to whether the delay was unintentional and may require further information as to the cause of the delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid delay in consideration of the merits, applicants should include a showing as to how the delay between first notification and petition filing was 'unintentional.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may require showing of when applicant became aware if petition not filed within 1 year
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a petition pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137 is not filed within 1 year of the date of abandonment, the Office may require further information as to when the applicant (or representative) first became aware of the abandonment and a showing as to how the delay in discovering the abandoned status occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should include the date they first became aware of abandonment and an explanation of how discovery of the abandoned status occurred to avoid delay in consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof on applicant to establish unintentional delay
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is a question whether the entire delay was unintentional, the Office may require the applicant to carry the burden of proof to establish that the delay was unintentional within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. 27 and 37 CFR 1.137.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While often the Office will accept the required statement alone, questions of intentionality trigger a need for evidence/argument to meet the burden; see Application of G and related case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which party's delay is relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: The relevant delay under 37 CFR 1.137 is that of the party having the right or authority to reply to avoid abandonment (or to not reply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant has assigned all right/title/interest to a third party, the applicant's delay is irrelevant. If a third party controls prosecution (partial assignee, licensee, employer), the third party's decision binds the applicant unless the third party is acting solely in a fiduciary capacity or the application was reassigned to the applicant before the reply due date. Contract terms that give the third party unbridled discretion bind the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer requirement for petitions under 37 CFR 1.137(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.137(d) requires that a petition under 37 CFR 1.137 be accompanied by a terminal disclaimer (and fee) in specified situations: (A) design applications; (B) nonprovisional utility applications (other than reissue) filed before June 8, 1995; (C) nonprovisional plant applications (other than reissue) filed before June 8, 1995; and certain applications filed on or after June 8, 1995 but before May 29, 2000 where abandonment occurred during appeal, interference, or secrecy order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The terminal disclaimer must dedicate to the public a terminal part of the patent term equivalent to the period of abandonment or (for pre-1995 utility/plant) the lesser of the period of abandonment or the period extending beyond twenty years from the U.S. filing date (or earliest priority date under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c)). The Office will not indicate the period disclaimed when granting revival. Filing a terminal disclaimer is not a substitute for showing unintentional delay, nor does unintentional delay waive the terminal disclaimer requirement. Applicants seeking waiver may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.183, but relief is strictly limited to 'extraordinary situations' where 'justice requires' it (e.g., abandonment that caused no actual delay). See MPEP § 1490.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for reconsideration timing and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.137(e) requires that any request for reconsideration or review of a decision refusing to revive an abandoned application must be filed within 2 months of the decision (or within such time as set in the decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless indicated otherwise, the time period for requesting reconsideration may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136. Renewed petitions, requests for reconsideration, or other petitions filed outside the time period may prompt the Office to require a specific showing as to how the entire delay was 'unintentional.' Intentional delays caused by deliberate choices remain immaterial to such requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of 37 CFR 1.137 to provisional applications and 12-month limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.137 applies to a provisional application abandoned for failure to reply to an Office requirement; a petition under 37 CFR 1.137(a) must be accompanied by any outstanding reply to an Office requirement. However, 35 U.S.C. 111(b)(5) provides that a provisional application shall be regarded as abandoned 12 months after its filing date and shall not be subject to revival after such 12-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition may be filed to revive a provisional application to establish pendency only for a period up to 12 months from the filing date. Even if revival is granted, the provisional application will not be considered pending after 12 months from filing. Note that the 12-month period is extended to the next business day if it falls on a weekend or federal holiday (35 U.S.C. 119(e)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's statement on petition to set aside examiner's holding (37 CFR 1.181)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.181 states that the examiner 'may be directed by the Director to furnish a written statement, within a specific time, setting forth the reasons for his or her decision upon the matters averred in the petition, supplying a copy to the petitioner.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless requested, such a statement should not be prepared (see MPEP § 1002.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to abandoned published and unpublished applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to the application file for any non-Image File Wrapper (IFW) abandoned published application may be available through the Patent and Trademark Copy Fulfillment Branch's Certified Copy Center (CCC). Access to an abandoned unpublished application may be provided to any person if a written request identifying or relying upon the abandoned application is submitted and the application is identified in specified documents (e.g., a U.S. patent application publication or patent, statutory invention registration, or published international application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of application-as-filed, file contents, or specific documents can be provided upon written request and payment of fees per 37 CFR 1.19(b). Form PTO/SB/68 may be used to request access under 37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(iv). Contact info and hours for CCC are provided. Identification must appear in the text of the citing document (application number, inventor, serial number and filing date, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of abandonment and computation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of abandonment is after midnight of the date on which the shortened statutory period (including any extensions under 37 CFR 1.136) expired; normally the end of the 3-month shortened statutory period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should scrutinize applications to verify abandonment and check for PBAs/Board decisions with allowed claims. Multiple examples are provided showing how abandonment date shifts with mailing dates, weekends, and federal holidays; instructions reference 35 U.S.C. 21 and 37 CFR 1.7 and MPEP § 710.05 for extensions to the next business day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering patented and abandoned paper and IFW files
rubrics_metrics.description: Recently patented and abandoned paper files are stored at the Files Repository; older files are in off-site warehouses. Image File Wrapper (IFW) applications are stored electronically; the electronic file is the official record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files are ordered via the File Ordering System (FOS) requiring delivery organization, employee number, and patent/application numbers. The FOS response indicates statuses: (A) accepted; (B) accepted but stored off-site; (C) not accepted — file not located; (D) not accepted — previous request not yet filled; (E) not accepted — invalid number. For IFW applications, physical delivery steps are not necessary. Drawings are generally stored within the application file and delivered together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifying applicants of abandonment and correspondence address responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Examining Corps currently mails a Notice of Abandonment (form PTOL-1432) to the correspondence address of record in all applications which become abandoned for failure to prosecute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mere failure to receive the notice does not affect the status of an abandoned application. Applicants must promptly file a paper notifying the Office of any change of address in each affected application (except under Customer Number practice). See MPEP §§ 403 and 601.03(a)-(b) for change-of-address procedures. Prompt action after receiving a notice is necessary; delay may preclude relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview policy and recordation (37 CFR 1.133 and Interview Best Practices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews between applicants (or practitioners) and examiners that improve mutual understanding of specific issues should be promoted; all discussions regarding the merits of a pending application are considered interviews and must be made of record (including electronic communications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews should be conducted with decorum and courtesy, efficiently, and within reasonable time. 37 CFR 1.133 requires interviews concerning applications to be conducted on Office premises and within Office hours as designated by examiners unless Director authorizes otherwise. An interview on patentability will not occur before the first Office action unless the application is continuing/substitute or the examiner determines it will advance prosecution. The examiner may require scheduling. If reconsideration is requested in view of an interview, a complete written statement of the reasons presented at the interview must be filed. Face-to-face interviews may be via video conferencing or in-person; telephone interviews may be appropriate; requests for face-to-face will normally be granted. Interview Best Practices and recordation guidance are available at www.uspto.gov/InterviewPractice.
